answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The forge is the collateral at risk, the quartz the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the horizon the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many quartz groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the forge into smaller, individually useless stakes.
